dedupe_keys.name: yongin severance hospital digital twin virtual hospital for it outage disaster response training

description: This case study builds and evaluates a digital twin of a hospital to train staff for a major information technology outage, when electronic medical records and clinical systems stop working. The authors published it as an open-access journal article about Yongin Severance Hospital in South Korea. The virtual hospital models 317 clinical spaces and 6 building entrances, and staff from several departments carried out a level 1 IT outage scenario in the virtual environment, switching to downtime procedures while quantitative performance metrics and survey feedback were collected. Coverage is a single hospital. The article is free under a Creative Commons Attribution licence; the platform itself is not published as software. Caveats: it is a proof of concept with one scenario, and the authors identified technical gaps in user permissions and prescription classification that must be solved before institutional deployment. The study found that the platform supported complete multi-department workflow execution for IT disaster response training, and participants highlighted realism, collaboration and prescription handling as key themes. Simulation uses: an example of a hospital digital twin for emergency response training against cyber attacks and technological failures. Related records: HospiT-Win (platform-hospit-win-patient-pathway-digital-twin) is an open platform for patient-pathway digital twins.
